headword: {長編小説|ちょうへんしょうせつ}
reading: ちょうへんしょうせつ

definitions.explanation: A lengthy work of fiction, typically several hundred pages or more. Distinguished from short stories and novellas by its scope and length.

examples.japanese: {長編小説|ちょうへんしょうせつ}を{読|よ}み{終|お}えた。
examples.english: I finished reading a full-length novel.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{初|はじ}めて{長編小説|ちょうへんしょうせつ}に{挑戦|ちょうせん}した。
examples.english: He attempted a full-length novel for the first time.

examples.japanese: この{作家|さっか}の{長編小説|ちょうへんしょうせつ}は{上下|じょうげ}{二巻|にかん}で{出版|しゅっぱん}された。
examples.english: This author's novel was published in two volumes.

notes:
Composed of {長編|ちょうへん} (long piece) + {小説|しょうせつ} (novel, fiction). The counterpart to {短編小説|たんぺんしょうせつ} (short story).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長編小説|ちょうへんしょうせつ}を{書|か}く: to write a full-length novel
- {長編小説|ちょうへんしょうせつ}に{挑戦|ちょうせん}する: to attempt a full-length novel
- {大河|たいが}{長編小説|ちょうへんしょうせつ}: epic novel, saga

RELATED WORDS:
- {短編小説|たんぺんしょうせつ}: short story
- {中編小説|ちゅうへんしょうせつ}: novella, medium-length fiction
- {長編|ちょうへん}: long piece (can also refer to long films, manga series, etc.)
- {大作|たいさく}: masterwork, major work — emphasizes ambition and scale

USAGE:
Often abbreviated to {長編|ちょうへん} when the context makes it clear fiction is being discussed.
